newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa shaves losses as origin selling abates.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa shaves losses as origin selling abates.

text.p: London's March cocoa futures approached the slippery zone of 865 stg on Tuesday but selling abated in time for the market to pare its losses.

Traders said sterling's strength against the French franc early on prompted a wave of selling from African origins whose currencies are linked to the franc, especially the Ivory Coast, but they stepped back as the parity weakened.
"There was selling from origins because of the currency but once the selling subsided prices began to recover," said one trader.

Benchmark March cocoa finished comfortably above its session low of 868, negating its life low of 865 as it ended six stg down on the day at 874 stg a tonne but traders said a new test of 865 was still conceivable while the downtrend remained intact.
A breach of 865 is likely to drag March to a fresh 18-month low of 847 based on key supply bands on the second month continuation chart.

Arbitrage hunters provided some support as they tapped the margin between London and New York but traders said a close in CSCE March below $1,322 would spawn bearish signals. At London's close it was at $1,318, down $11.
London's turnover totalled 4,405 lots including AA and switches. The key March/May structure weakened to 22 stg.

Traders are curiously awaiting new arrival figures from West Africa to make sense of forecasters' views on supply prospects. The early crop came in low numbers but analysts are expecting a recovery in January after favourable weather.
The bets on March also involve possible maneouverings of one trade house believed to hold a large volume of physical cocoa delivered to it in September.
In other news, confectionery industry representatives were getting ready for a key annual event in Cologne which this year runs between January 26-30. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom 44-171-542 8072
